name: Sila Nanotechnologies
short_description: Makes silicon anode materials that raise battery energy density.
why_relevant: Dropped-in silicon anodes proven inside Mercedes-Benz vehicles.
history: Sila Nanotechnologies was founded in 2011 in Alameda, California by Gene Berdichevsky, Alex Jacobs and Gleb Yushin to commercialize silicon anode chemistry. Its Titan material progressed from lab samples to automotive qualification, and in 2021 the company raised over 500 million dollars at a 3.3 billion dollar valuation. Sila opened a large Moses Lake, Washington factory in 2024 and began shipping Titan silicon to Mercedes-Benz for the electric G-Class. Today Sila is ramping production and licensing its anode platform to battery makers worldwide.

name: Group14 Technologies
short_description: Produces SCC55 silicon-carbon composite anodes at scale.
why_relevant: Factory-scaled anode chemistry reusable across e-mobility and air taxis.
history: Group14 Technologies was founded in 2015 in Woodinville, Washington by Rick Costantino and Aaron Feaver to scale a silicon-carbon composite anode. Its SCC55 material attracted backing from Porsche, SK Inc. and Microsoft's climate fund, and the company built one of the world's largest anode active-material plants in Moses Lake, Washington. A joint venture with SK in South Korea extended production to Asia, while acquisitions secured the silicon feedstock supply chain. Today Group14 supplies automotive and consumer battery customers and continues expanding capacity for e-mobility and electric aviation.

name: Lyten
short_description: Tunable 3D graphene platform for batteries, composites and sensors.
why_relevant: One material platform spanning energy to defense structural parts.
history: Lyten was founded in 2015 in San Jose, California to commercialize a tunable three-dimensional graphene platform. The company developed lithium-sulfur batteries, composites and sensors from the same material, drawing investment from Stellantis, FedEx and Honeywell. It opened a lithium-sulfur pilot line and, in 2024, acquired Cuberg's lithium-metal assets from Northvolt to accelerate its energy roadmap. Lyten also announced plans for a large lithium-sulfur gigafactory in Nevada. Today it is positioned across energy storage, lightweight composites and defense structural applications.

name: SixPoint Materials
short_description: Grows low-defect GaN crystals for next-gen power electronics.
why_relevant: Substrate quality underpinning efficiency gains in power semiconductors.
history: SixPoint Materials was founded in 2007 in Buellton, California to produce low-defect bulk gallium nitride crystals using hydride vapor phase epitaxy. The company focused on native GaN substrates that outperform sapphire and silicon for power and RF devices, an enabling layer for efficient power electronics. It has supplied research and industrial customers and pursued partnerships across the power semiconductor supply chain. Today SixPoint remains a specialist substrate developer supporting the shift toward higher-efficiency GaN-based devices in data centers, vehicles and renewable-energy converters.

name: Metalenz
short_description: Replaces traditional lenses with flat meta-optics in cameras and sensors.
why_relevant: Flattened the camera lens across phones, cars and face unlock systems.
history: Metalenz was founded in 2016 in Boston as a spin-out of Federico Capasso's Harvard metasurface research by Rob Devlin and colleagues. It pioneered flat meta-optics that replace stacked lenses with a single patterned surface, and partnered with STMicroelectronics to manufacture the devices in high volume. The company shipped millions of metasurface units into consumer devices and expanded into polarization sensing and 3D imaging. Today Metalenz supplies meta-optics for smartphones, automotive systems and biometric face-unlock platforms, and continues to push optical functions onto silicon.

name: General Graphene
short_description: Commercial-scale production method for single-layer graphene rolls.
why_relevant: Turns graphene from lab wonder into an industrial roll-to-roll material.
history: General Graphene was founded in 2017 in Knoxville, Tennessee to industrialize single-layer graphene production. Its rapid thermal chemical vapor deposition process enabled continuous roll-to-roll manufacturing, turning graphene from a laboratory curiosity into a specifiable industrial material. The company scaled its lines and supplied graphene films to electronics, sensors and coatings developers. Backed by private investment, it focused on cost reduction and consistent quality. Today General Graphene is one of the few producers capable of delivering large-area graphene at commercial volume and is expanding applications across composites and energy devices.

name: Natrion
short_description: Develops lithium-metal solid-state ions with a scalable process.
why_relevant: Cost-effective solid-state architecture requiring no cleanroom coating.
history: Natrion was founded in 2018 in Vestal, New York, spun out of research at Binghamton University by Alex Kosyakov. The company developed a lithium-ionic solid electrolyte and a lithium-metal solid-state architecture designed to work without cleanroom coating, targeting a cheaper route to solid-state batteries. It raised seed and Series A funding, won defense and energy research contracts, and demonstrated cells with improved safety and energy density. Today Natrion is scaling its solid-state platform with manufacturing partners and positioning it for electric vehicles, aviation and portable electronics.

name: Skeleton Technologies
short_description: Graphene-based ultracapacitors and next-gen high-voltage cell stacks.
why_relevant: Of the highest-energy ultracapacitors used in heavy transport and grids.
history: Skeleton Technologies was founded in 2009 in Tallinn, Estonia by Taavi Madiberk and Oliver Ahlberg to build high-energy ultracapacitors. Using carbide-derived carbon and curved graphene, it developed cells among the most energy-dense in their class and supplied heavy transport, grid and industrial customers. The company raised substantial growth capital, opened a plant in Germany and unveiled its SuperBattery concept for hybrid storage. Today Skeleton is expanding manufacturing and targeting buses, trucks and grid applications where rapid charging and long life matter more than raw capacity.

name: Nanobiotix
short_description: Nanoparticle radioenhancers that boost radiation therapy inside tumors.
why_relevant: First-in-class physics-based anti-cancer approach approved in humans.
history: Nanobiotix was founded in 2003 in Paris by Laurent Levy to develop nanoparticle radioenhancers for cancer therapy. Its lead product, based on hafnium oxide nanoparticles, concentrates radiation dose inside tumors and became the first such approach approved for human use in Europe for soft tissue sarcoma. The company listed on Euronext, signed licensing deals in Asia and formed a collaboration with Janssen for head and neck cancer. Today Nanobiotix is advancing clinical programs across multiple tumor types and expanding its physics-based oncology platform worldwide.

name: Nth Cycle
short_description: Electro-extraction platform producing critical minerals from mine waste.
why_relevant: Refines nickel and cobalt without smelters, on-site at the mine.
history: Nth Cycle was founded in 2017 by Megan O'Connor to refine critical metals without smelters. Its electro-extraction platform recovers nickel, cobalt and other minerals from mine tailings, spent catalysts and battery scrap, producing feedstocks on site at the mine or recycler. The company raised venture funding, opened a commercial-scale facility and won defense and clean-energy contracts. Today Nth Cycle is scaling its modular refining units to strengthen domestic supply chains for the energy transition and reduce the environmental footprint of conventional metal processing.

name: Ecovative Design
short_description: Grows packaging and textile materials from mycelium instead of plastic.
why_relevant: Compostable material grown in days to replace expanded-foam packaging.
history: Ecovative Design was founded in 2007 in Green Island, New York by Eben Bayer and Gavin McIntyre to grow materials from mycelium. Its compostable biocomposites replaced expanded-foam packaging for major brands, and the company expanded into textile and food applications. It spun off MyForest Foods for mycelium-based meat alternatives and built partnerships across packaging and fashion. Today Ecovative licenses its growth platform and produces mycelium materials at scale, positioning biology as a sustainable manufacturing route for everyday products.

name: Molg
short_description: Installs robotic additive manufacturing using PEEK materials in space.
why_relevant: Printing parts in orbit beats fragile shipping launches for small modules.
history: Molg was founded in 2020 to enable robotic assembly and additive manufacturing in space. Its system installs modular robotic cells that 3D-print PEEK parts in orbit, allowing satellites and space stations to manufacture components on demand instead of shipping fragile hardware through launch. The company raised early-stage funding and demonstrated its technology with space and defense partners. Today Molg is developing in-space manufacturing services intended to cut launch mass, extend mission life and open new orbital industrial applications.

name: Graphenea
short_description: European producer of graphene films and powders for industry.
why_relevant: EU anchor for reliable, spec-controlled graphene supply.
history: Graphenea was founded in 2010 in San Sebastián, Spain as a spin-out of the CIC nanoGUNE research center. It became a European producer of chemical vapor deposition graphene films and graphene oxide powders, serving electronics, sensors and materials researchers with spec-controlled supply. The company expanded its production capacity, opened a US subsidiary and built a broad industrial customer base. Today Graphenea is a reference supplier for reliable graphene, supporting the transition of the material from academic study into commercial devices and composites.

name: Notpla
short_description: Makes seaweed-based packaging from condiment sachets to takeaway boxes.
why_relevant: Plastic-free packaging that biodegrades in weeks, proven with festivals.
history: Notpla was founded in 2014 in London by Pierre Paslier and Rodrigo Garcia Gonzalez to replace single-use plastic with seaweed-based materials. It launched edible Ooho sachets, then scaled coatings and takeaway packaging used at major sporting and music events. The company won the Earthshot Prize in 2022 and raised significant funding to expand production. Today Notpla supplies plastic-free packaging that biodegrades in weeks and is working to bring seaweed materials into mainstream food and beverage service.

name: Living Ink
short_description: Turns algae biomass into inks that replace carbon black pigment.
why_relevant: Prints carbon-aware products whose ink color comes from living cells.
history: Living Ink was founded in 2014 in Boulder, Colorado to turn algae biomass into sustainable pigments. Its Algae Black ink replaces petroleum-derived carbon black in printing and packaging, giving brands a lower-carbon option without sacrificing performance. The company scaled production, partnered with major consumer-goods and packaging firms, and expanded its color range. Today Living Ink supplies bio-based inks for textiles, labels and packaging, positioning algae as a renewable feedstock for the colorants industry.

name: Amprius Technologies
short_description: High-energy silicon-anode cells with the highest claimed specific energy.
why_relevant: Enables high-altitude flight and aerospace with 450 Wh/kg cells.
history: Amprius Technologies was founded in 2008 in Fremont, California, spun out of Stanford research by Yi Cui to commercialize silicon nanowire anodes. Its cells reached 450 Wh/kg, among the highest specific energies in production, and found use in high-altitude flight and aerospace. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022, opened a large-scale manufacturing facility and shipped cells for defense and aviation customers. Today Amprius is scaling production and developing higher-energy chemistries for electric aviation, drones and specialty applications.

name: Enovix
short_description: Brake the battery mold to pack more silicon into the same footprint.
why_relevant: Cell architecture that boosts energy while keeping standard dimensions.
history: Enovix was founded in 2007 to commercialize a three-dimensional silicon battery architecture that packs more energy into a standard footprint. Its braided electrode design uses a 100 percent silicon anode while managing swelling and safety. The company listed on Nasdaq in 2021, built a high-volume factory in Malaysia and signed agreements with consumer-electronics and automotive customers. Today Enovix is ramping production of its next-generation cells for smartphones, wearables and electric vehicles, targeting higher energy density without changing device dimensions.

name: OneD Battery Sciences
short_description: Adds silicon nanowires to standard graphite anodes via SINANODE.
why_relevant: Upgrades existing gigafactories to 50 percent more energy without new lines.
history: OneD Battery Sciences was founded in 2009 in Sunnyvale, California to boost lithium-ion energy using silicon nanowires. Its SINANODE process grows nanowires directly onto graphite inside existing anode manufacturing, raising energy by roughly fifty percent without new production lines. Backed by venture funding and a strategic partnership with General Motors, the company advanced its technology toward automotive qualification. Today OneD is commercializing SINANODE as a drop-in upgrade for gigafactories seeking higher energy density at lower cost.

name: Sion Power
short_description: Develops high-energy lithium-sulfur cells for aviation and defense.
why_relevant: Decades of Li-S work now aimed at the aerospace energy density gap.
history: Sion Power traces its origins to 1994 in Tucson, Arizona, where it began as Moltech developing lithium-sulfur batteries. After licensing related technology and surviving years of restructuring, it refocused on high-energy Li-S cells for aviation and defense, where weight savings are critical. The company built pilot manufacturing and demonstrated cells with substantially higher specific energy than conventional lithium-ion. Today Sion Power is scaling its Licerion lithium-metal technology with aerospace partners, aiming to close the energy-density gap for electric flight and long-endurance platforms.

name: Aspen Aerogels
short_description: Produces the world's best-known aerogel insulation for energy and EV thermal barriers.
why_relevant: Insulates battery packs while the same material insulates LNG facilities.
history: Aspen Aerogels was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Northborough, Massachusetts. It commercialized aerogel blankets that insulate industrial facilities, LNG plants and, increasingly, electric-vehicle battery packs. The company went public on the NYSE in 2014 and later launched its PyroThin thermal barriers, winning contracts with major automakers. Today Aspen Aerogels operates expanded manufacturing and positions its aerogel materials across energy infrastructure, EV safety and building applications, with automotive thermal barriers driving much of its growth.

name: View
short_description: Electrochromic glass that tints in seconds to control heat and light.
why_relevant: Building-integrated photonics that cut HVAC energy by a fifth.
history: View was founded in 2007 in Milpitas, California, originally as Soladigm, to develop electrochromic glass. Its dynamic windows tint in seconds to control heat and glare, cutting cooling demand and improving comfort in commercial buildings. The company went public on Nasdaq in 2020 and installed its glass in offices, airports and hospitals across North America. After restructuring, it refocused on manufacturing and profitability. Today View continues to supply building-integrated smart glass as energy codes and decarbonization goals drive demand for efficient facades.

name: NanoXplore
short_description: TSX-listed producer of graphene powders used in plastics and concrete.
why_relevant: Ton-scale graphene masterbatch integrated into industrial polymers.
history: NanoXplore was founded in 2011 in Montreal, Quebec, and became a leading producer of graphene powders and masterbatches. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, it integrated graphene into plastics, composites and concrete and expanded through acquisitions in compounding and molding. The company serves automotive, packaging and industrial customers seeking lighter, stronger materials. Today NanoXplore operates ton-scale production and continues to develop graphene-enhanced products, positioning itself as a vertically integrated supplier bridging nanomaterials and large-volume manufacturing.

name: Undagrid
short_description: 3D-prints concrete reinforcement from recycled plastic.
why_relevant: Doubles the lifespan of slabs with corrosion-proof plastic meshes.
history: Undagrid was founded in 2015 in Delft, the Netherlands, to replace steel reinforcement in concrete with 3D-printed plastic. Its Raptor mesh is additively manufactured from recycled plastic and resists corrosion, extending the service life of slabs and reducing maintenance. The company won construction-industry awards, ran pilot projects with builders and infrastructure partners, and refined its automated printing process. Today Undagrid is scaling its additive rebar technology as the construction sector seeks durable, low-carbon alternatives to traditional steel reinforcement.

name: Vantablack-first maker Surrey NanoSystems
short_description: Maker of Vantablack and low-emissivity coatings for optics and sensors.
why_relevant: Ultra-black materials suppress stray light in telescopes and spacecraft.
history: Surrey NanoSystems was founded in 2006 in Newhaven, United Kingdom, to commercialize vertically aligned carbon nanotube coatings. It created Vantablack, one of the darkest materials ever made, and applied super-black and low-emissivity coatings to optics, sensors and spacecraft, where suppressing stray light is critical. The company supplied space and defense customers and continued developing its nanotube deposition processes. Today Surrey NanoSystems remains a specialist in ultra-black materials and advanced coatings, supporting astronomy, imaging and thermal-control applications.

name: Phospholutions
short_description: RhizoSorb increases phosphorus efficiency so less fertilizer washes into water.
why_relevant: Squeezes more yield from the same fertilizer while cleaning runoff.
history: Phospholutions was founded in 2015 in State College, Pennsylvania, as a spin-out of Penn State research by Hunter Swisher. Its RhizoSorb technology improves phosphorus uptake by crops, allowing farmers to use less fertilizer while maintaining yields and reducing runoff into waterways. The company raised venture funding, won agricultural innovation awards and expanded field trials across North America. Today Phospholutions is commercializing RhizoSorb with fertilizer and retail partners, addressing both food security and water-quality challenges in modern agriculture.

name: 6K Additive
short_description: Microwave plasma atomization produces premium metal powders from scrap.
why_relevant: Fuels additive manufacturing with lower-carbon, equivalent powders.
history: 6K Additive was established in 2014 as part of 6K, based in North Andover, Massachusetts, to produce advanced metal powders. Its UniMelt microwave plasma platform converts scrap and feedstock into premium spherical powders for additive manufacturing, offering lower carbon intensity than conventional atomization. The company expanded capacity, qualified alloys for aerospace and defense, and built a recycling business for titanium and nickel. Today 6K Additive supplies the growing 3D-printing market with sustainable, high-performance powders.
